English.question:
১) 1) Questions 1-30 : Replace the underlined part(s) of each sentence with the option which is grammatically correct. If no replacement is needed, choose ‘A’.
I don’t agree with your proposal.
English.exp:
Agree with- কারো সাথে একমত হওয়া, Agree to- কারো প্রস্তাবে রাজি হওয়া, Agree on- কোনো বিষয়ে একমত হওয়া .
I don’t agree to your proposal.

English.question: 2) <u>As soon as</u> it stopped raining when we started our journey.
English.exp: If there is 'when' then the sentence will start with 'Hardly'. Hardly had it stopped raining when we started our journey.

English.question: 3) By the end of summer, you <u>will pass</u> your higher secondary examination.
English.exp:
Sentence is in Future perfect tense.
Subject + will/shall + have + V3 + extension.
By the end of summer, you will have passed your higher secondary examination.

English.question: 4) It’s 8:30 o’clock now. His paper starts at 9. He <u>is writing</u> answers at 9:30.
English.exp:
Sentence is in Future continuous tense.
Subject + will/shall + be + V-ing + extension.
It’s 8:30 o’clock now. His paper starts at 9. He will be writing answers at 9:30.

English.question: 5) <u>A little</u> water was in a jug so a crow survived.
English.exp: Few is a quantifier used with plural countable nouns. Little is used with singular uncountable nouns. And when we say 'a little' or 'a few’, we mean a small amount, but it's enough. Water is singular uncountable noun. So, a little should be used here. A little water was in a jug so a crow survived.

English.question: 6) <u>Some</u> work has been done yet. What about the remaining work?
English.exp: little, a little, the little, less- uncountable noun এর ক্ষেত্রে ব্যবহৃত হয়। Work is singular uncountable noun.

English.question: 7) A festival of kites <u>was</u> very famous at Old Dhaka.
English.exp: When you are speaking of or for yourself, use 'am.' When you are talking about a person or a thing (in the singular), use 'is.' When you are talking to a person, and when you are talking about other people or things (in the plural), use 'are.' Here, 'A festival' is singular. Hence, ‘is’ will be used. 'was' won't be the answer because it's still a famous festival.

English.question: 8) The police made him <u>confess</u> his crime.
English.exp:
Confess - admit that one has committed a crime or done something wrong.
Make + Person + base form of verb

English.question: 9) If she had worked hard, she <u>will elect</u> in the election.
English.exp: If এর ক্ষেত্রে একটি Clause Past Perfect হলে, অন্যটি would/could/might + have + verb-এর p.p. form - এই অনুযায়ী গঠিত হবে।

English.question: 10) Neither of the biscuits you gave me <u>is contain</u> chocolate chips.
English.exp: 'is contain' and 'are contained' will make a grammatically incorrect sentence. 'contain' is used with singular nouns. Hence 'contains' is the right choice.

English.question: 11) You <u>should have take</u> permission of your parents before taking this important decision.
English.exp:
Sentence is in Future perfect tense and active voice.
Subject + modal verb + have/has + V3 + extension.
You should have taken permission of your parents before taking this important decision.

English.question: 12) The husband and wife stood <u>beside</u> each other as they shook hands with the guests.
English.exp: Beside- at the side of; next to.

English.question: 13) I have never gone to Japan. I know <u>few</u> people there.
English.exp: Few is a quantifier used with plural countable nouns. People are plural countable noun.

English.question: 14) I am a doctor <u>when</u> my wife is a nurse.
English.exp:
while - whereas (indicating a contrast).
I am a doctor while my wife is a nurse.

English.question: 15) Dalia <u>was talking</u> since she arrived.
English.exp: In case of ‘since’, the structure should be- Present Indefinite/Present perfect+Past Indefinite

English.question: 16) Does she <u>have to</u> get up early and cook for family at this old age?
English.exp: As ‘does’ is used in the interrogative sentence, we have to use the base form of the auxiliary verb after the subject.

English.question: 17) He reminds us <u>about</u> Paul Walker.
English.exp: 'Reminds of' someone.

English.question: 18) If Rahim hadn't argued, Alam <u>lost</u> the case.
English.exp: If এর ক্ষেত্রে একটি Clause Past Perfect হলে, অন্যটি would/could/might + have + verb-এর p.p. form - এই অনুযায়ী গঠিত হবে।

English.question: 19) In olden days, doves <u>take</u> messages.
English.exp: By using 'took' a simple past tense sentence can be made. Other options make a grammatically incorrect sentence.

English.question: 20) He was accustomed <u>of</u> chewing gum even when he delivered the lecture.
English.exp: Accustomed means to get used to something or become familiar with.'To' is the correct preposition to use after accustomed.

English.question: 21) When she arrived home after a hard day at work, her husband <u>was sleeping</u>.
English.exp: When+Past Indefinite+Past Continuous.

English.question: 22) That child died <u>at</u> heavy fever.
English.exp:
die at (time): He died at 9–30 a.m.
die within (time): He died within five minutes.
die of (disease): He died of cholera.
die from (effect): He died from snake bite/ overeating.
die in (accident): He died in a train accident.

English.question: 23) He <u>burnt</u> his fingers by interfering in his neighbour’s affairs.
English.exp: burnt his fingers - to suffer unpleasant results of an action.

English.question: 24) He is <u>a</u> union leader.
English.exp: 'The' is a definite article which is used before a noun that is fixed or special or discussed earlier. 'A/An' is used before an indefinite singular noun. 'Union leader' is a fixed noun. Hence 'the' will be used.

English.question: 25) It is shady <u>below</u> the tree.
English.exp: Under is used when something is directly under another. Below is preferred when something is in a lower position.

English.question: 26) What time did you arrive <u>in</u> the station?
English.exp: Always use 'at' to express arrival at a small place.

English.question: 27) He <u>was died</u> in a fight with some drunken sailors.
English.exp: নিজে মারা যাওয়া অর্থে die ব্যবহৃত হয়। নিহত হওয়া অর্থে kill এর Passive form ব্যবহৃত হয়। He was killed in a fight with some drunken sailors.

English.question: 28) Mr. John <u>settled</u> in Dhaka since his wife died.
English.exp:
Sentence is in Present perfect tense with active voice.
Subject + has/have + V3 + extension.

English.question: 29) Neha was angry <u>about</u> herself for making such a stupid mistake.
English.exp: If directed at a person 'angry with' should always be used.

English.question: 30) He has killed his own father. He is in jail because of <u>prolicide</u>.
English.exp: Patricide- the killing of one's father.

English.question:
31) Questions 31-55 : Identify the missing word/phrase from the given choices.
We are moved not by the fall of great man but the elevation to heroism of what we had taken to be a little man.
English.exp:
Subject+verb+ a/an+adjective+singular noun.
We are moved not by the fall of a great man but the elevation to heroism of what we had taken to be a little man.

English.question: 32) He is in temper.
English.exp:
He is in a temper.
Example of some similar phrases- in a body, in a hurry, in a nutshell, in a fix.

English.question: 33) My house is comfortable than my father’s.
English.exp:
‘very’ is used before positive degree and ‘much/very much’ is used before comparative degree.
My house is much more comfortable than my father’s.

English.question: 34) Samir is smaller of the two boys.
English.exp:
Subject+verb+the+comparative+of+the+two+plural noun.
Samir is the smaller of the two boys.

English.question: 35) The committee voted to ratify the amendment the objections.
English.exp:
কোন কিছু সত্বেও অর্থে in spite of/despite ব্যবহৃত হয়। Despite এর পরে কখনোই of বসে না।
The committee voted to ratify the amendment despite the objections.

English.question: 36) Penicillin continues to be used widely, some strains of bacteria have developed a resistance to the drug.
English.exp:
Although/Though এর অর্থ যদিও, কিছু হওয়া সত্ত্বেও।
Although Penicillin continues to be used widely, some strains of bacteria have developed a resistance to the drug.

English.question: 37) Hospitable people like speaking to foreigners even they have not been introduced.
English.exp:
কোন কিছু ঘটা সত্ত্বেও অন্য পরিস্থিতি একই থাকে সেক্ষেত্রে যদিও/তবুও অর্থে even if ব্যবহৃত হয়।
Hospitable people like speaking to foreigners even if they have not been introduced.

English.question: 38) Nothing can absolve you the promise you have made.
English.exp:
Absolve from- দোষ, প্রতিশ্রুতি থেকে মুক্ত করা।
Nothing can absolve you from the promise you have made.

English.question: 39) Sumon accommodated me a loan.
English.exp:
Accommodated with- সাহায্য করা।
Sumon accommodated me with a loan.

English.question: 40) It's impolite to break when someone else is talking.
English.exp:
Break in- বাধা দেয়া।
It's impolite to break in when someone else is talking.

English.question: 41) He brought a new edition of his book.
English.exp:
Brought out- ছেপে প্রকাশ করা।
He brought out a new edition of his book.

English.question: 42) Do not carry anything without considering everything.
English.exp:
Carry out- সম্পাদন করা, পালন করা।
Do not carry out anything without considering everything.

English.question: 43) We should do away our bad habits.
English.exp:
Do away with- বাতিল করা বা বিলোপ করা।
We should do away with our bad habits.

English.question: 44) As this is his first job, he will have to put up the inconvenience.
English.exp:
Put up with- সহ্য করা।
As this is his first job, he will have to put up with the inconvenience.

English.question: 45) They yet to make a decision.
English.exp:
কোন কিছু এখনো করা হয়নি অর্থে have/has yet to ব্যবহৃত হয়।
They have yet to make a decision.

English.question: 46) His furniture, including a dining table and six chairs, being sold.
English.exp:
Furniture is always followed by a singular verb as it is an uncountable noun.
His furniture, including a dining table and six chairs, is being sold.

English.question: 47) I am also your friend. Would you invite me your birthday celebration?
English.exp:
invite someone in- to ask someone to come into one’s house.
I am also your friend. Would you invite me in your birthday celebration?

English.question: 48) As soon as I came in, she left the room.
English.exp: অতীতকালের দুটি কাজ যদি as soon as দ্বারা যুক্ত থাকে তাহলে দুটি কাজই past indefinite tense এ হবে।

English.question: 49) No, I don’t have the details, but you can look it up on the internet.
English.exp: At my fingertips - readily available; accessible.

English.question: 50) Never before have the leaders of the country met in an earnest attempt to resolve their differences.
English.exp: বাক্যের শুরুতে Never before থাকলে inversion (Never before+auxiliary verb+subject+main verb) হয়।

English.question: 51) I suggested that he take legal advice.
English.exp:
Subject+suggest+that+subject+should (ব্যবহার করা যায় বা উহ্যও রাখা যায়)+base form of verb+extension.
I suggested that he should take legal advice.

English.question: 52) A teacher always prefer that her every single student speak the truth.
English.exp: Subject+prefer+that+subject+base form of verb+extension.

English.question: 53) The students went to the principal and requested that the examination be postponed.
English.exp: Subject+request+that+subject+base form of verb+extension. Be verb এর ক্ষেত্রে শুধু be বসবে।

English.question: 54) Not only whales among the largest animals that ever lived, but they are also among the most intelligent.
English.exp:
বাক্যের শুরুতে Not only থাকলে inversion (Not only+auxiliary verb+subject+main verb) হয়।
Not only are whales among the largest animals that ever lived, but they are also among the most intelligent.

English.question: 55) I will avail the opportunity.
English.exp:
avail oneself of- use or take advantage of (an opportunity or available resource).
I will avail myself of the opportunity.

English.question:
56) Questions 56-80 : Choose the answer that best expresses the same meaning of the given word.
RANT
English.exp:
Treat : behave towards or deal with in a certain way.
Noisy : making or given to making a lot of noise.
Formalize : give (something) legal or formal status.
Praise : express warm approval or admiration of.
Rant : speak or shout at length in an angry, impassioned way.

English.question: 57) CIVIL
English.exp:
Sophisticated : having, revealing, or involving a great deal of worldly experience and knowledge of fashion and culture.
Social : relating to society or its organization.
Formal : done in accordance with convention or etiquette; suitable for or constituting an official or important occasion.
Polite : having or showing behaviour that is respectful and considerate of other people.
Civil : courteous and polite.

English.question: 58) PREDICT
English.exp:
Determine : cause (something) to occur in a particular way or to have a particular nature.
Analyse : examine (something) methodically and in detail, typically in order to explain and interpret it.
Foretell : predict (the future or a future event).
Describe : give a detailed account in words of.
Predict : say or estimate that (a specified thing) will happen in the future or will be a consequence of something.

English.question: 59) OMINOUS
English.exp:
Poisonous : (of a substance or plant) causing or capable of causing death or illness if taken into the body.
Foregone : past.
Foreboding : a feeling that something bad will happen; fearful apprehension.
Bad : of poor quality or a low standard.
Ominous : giving the worrying impression that something bad is going to happen; threateningly inauspicious.

English.question: 60) FOSTER
English.exp:
Discourage : cause (someone) to lose confidence or enthusiasm.
Fabricate : invent (something) in order to deceive.
Foment : instigate or stir up (an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action).
Nurture : care for and protect (someone or something) while they are growing.
Foster : bring up (a child that is not one's own by birth).

English.question: 61) PROLIFIC
English.exp:
Plenty : a large or sufficient amount or quantity; more than enough.
Competent : having the necessary ability, knowledge, or skill to do something successfully.
Fertile : (of soil or land) producing or capable of producing abundant vegetation or crops.
Predominant : present as the strongest or main element.
Prolific : (of a plant, animal, or person) producing much fruit or foliage or many offspring.

English.question: 62) EFFETE
English.exp:
Affected : influenced or touched by an external factor.
Injured : harmed, damaged, or impaired.
Feeble : lacking physical strength, especially as a result of age or illness.
Sick : affected by physical or mental illness.
Effete : (of a man) weak or effeminate.

English.question: 63) IMPEDIMENT
English.exp:
Passage : the action or process of moving through or past somewhere on the way from one place to another.
Obstruction : the action of obstructing or the state of being obstructed.
Fateful : having far-reaching and often disastrous consequences or implications.
Destruction : the action or process of causing so much damage to something that it no longer exists or cannot be repaired.
Impediment : a hindrance or obstruction in doing something.

English.question: 64) AMNESTY
English.exp:
Revolt : take violent action against an established government or ruler; rebel.
Privilege : a special right, advantage, or immunity granted or available only to a particular person or group.
Farewell : used to express good wishes on parting.
Pardon : the action of forgiving or being forgiven for an error or offence.
Amnesty : an official pardon for people who have been convicted of political offences.

English.question: 65) LUMINARY
English.exp:
Bright : giving out or reflecting much light; shining.
Lightning : very quick.
Famous : known about by many people.
Dashing : (of a man) attractive, adventurous, and full of confidence.
Luminary : a person who inspires or influences others, especially one prominent in a particular sphere.

English.question: 66) ADVERSITY
English.exp:
Crisis : a time of intense difficulty or danger.
Misfortune : bad luck.
Failure : lack of success.
Helplessness : inability to defend oneself or to act effectively.
Adversity : a difficult or unpleasant situation.

English.question: 67) RECALL
English.exp:
Speak : say something in order to convey information or to express a feeling.
Receive : be given, presented with, or paid (something).
Face : the front part of a person's head from the forehead to the chin, or the corresponding part in an animal.
Remember : have in or be able to bring to one's mind an awareness of (someone or something from the past).
Recall : cause one to remember or think of.

English.question: 68) ULTERIOR
English.exp:
Revealed : make (previously unknown or secret information) known to others.
Implied : suggested but not directly expressed; implicit.
Extreme : reaching a high or the highest degree; very great.
Decisive : settling an issue; producing a definite result.
Ulterior : existing beyond what is obvious or admitted; intentionally hidden.

English.question: 69) EXCLUSIVE
English.exp:
Extensive : covering or affecting a large area.
Sole : the undersurface of a person's foot.
External : belonging to or forming the outer surface or structure of something.
Excessive : more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; immoderate.
Exclusive : restricted to the person, group, or area concerned.

English.question: 70) PORTRAY
English.exp:
Communicate : share or exchange information, news, or ideas.
Paint : a coloured substance which is spread over a surface and dries to leave a thin decorative or protective coating.
Express : convey (a thought or feeling) in words or by gestures and conduct.
Draw : produce (a picture or diagram) by making lines and marks on paper with a pencil, pen, etc.
Portray : depict (someone or something) in a work of art or literature.

English.question: 71) CONUNDRUM
English.exp:
Question : a sentence worded or expressed so as to elicit information.
Discussion : the action or process of talking about something in order to reach a decision or to exchange ideas.
Explanation : a statement or account that makes something clear.
Solution : a means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
Conundrum : a question asked for amusement, typically one with a pun in its answer; a riddle.

English.question: 72) INEVITABLE
English.exp:
Unavoidable : not able to be avoided, prevented, or ignored; inevitable.
Probable : likely to happen or be the case.
Expected : regarded as likely; anticipated.
Fixed : fastened securely in position.
Inevitable : certain to happen; unavoidable.

English.question: 73) DROWSY
English.exp:
Soothing : having a gently calming effect.
Lazy : unwilling to work or use energy.
Exhausted : very tired.
Sleepy : needing or ready for sleep.
Drowsy : sleepy and lethargic; half asleep.

English.question: 74) DEPLETE
English.exp:
Destroy : end the existence of (something) by damaging or attacking it.
Finish : bring (a task or activity) to an end; complete.
Exhaust : make (someone) feel very tired.
Vanish : disappear suddenly and completely.
Deplete : use up the supply or resources of.

English.question: 75) CAPITULATE
English.exp:
Surrender : stop resisting an enemy or opponent and submit to their authority.
Withdraw : remove or take away (something) from a particular place or position.
Execute : put (a plan, order, or course of action) into effect.
Summarize : give a brief statement of the main points of (something).
Capitulate : cease to resist an opponent or an unwelcome demand; yield.

English.question: 76) ABSTEMIOUS
English.exp:
Moderate : average in amount, intensity, quality, or degree.
Proud : feeling deep pleasure or satisfaction as a result of one's own achievements, qualities, or possessions or those of someone with whom one is closely associated.
Excessive : more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; immoderate.
Rustic : relating to the countryside; rural.
Abstemious : indulging only very moderately in something, especially food and drink.

English.question: 77) EXORBITANT
English.exp:
Odd : different to what is usual or expected; strange.
Ridiculous : deserving or inviting derision or mockery; absurd.
Excessive : more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; immoderate.
Threatening : having a hostile or deliberately frightening quality or manner.
Exorbitant : (of a price or amount charged) unreasonably high.

English.question: 78) OBTUSE
English.exp:
Distant : far away in space or time.
Blunt : (of a cutting implement) not having a sharp edge or point.
Excessive : more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; immoderate.
Vague : of uncertain, indefinite, or unclear character or meaning.
Obtuse : not sharp-pointed or sharp-edged; blunt.

English.question: 79) EGREGIOUS
English.exp:
Progressive : happening or developing gradually or in stages.
Superficial : existing or occurring at or on the surface.
Shocking : causing indignation or disgust; offensive.
Cowardly : lacking courage.
Egregious : outstandingly bad; shocking.

English.question: 80) EXOTIC
English.exp:
Beautiful : pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically.
Colourful : having much or varied colour; bright.
Excellent : extremely good; outstanding.
Unusual : remarkable or interesting because different from or better than others.
Exotic : attractive or striking because colourful or out of the ordinary.
